request.input:
Bill number: HB0039
<bill_text>
HOUSE BILL 39

 By Davis

 AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 5;
 Title 6; Title 7; Title 49 and Title 67, relative to the
 Menstrual Hygiene Products Accessibility Act.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-417, is amended by deleting the

section and substituting instead the following:

 (a) This section is known and may be cited as the "Menstrual Hygiene Products

 Accessibility Act."

 (b) As used in this section:

 (1) "Eligible school" means a public school, including a public charter

 school, that is a senior high school, as defined in § 49-6-401; and

 (2) "Feminine hygiene product":

 (A) Means a product or material designed for feminine hygiene in

 connection with menstruation or other genital-tract secretions; and

 (B) Includes tampons, panty liners, menstrual cups, sanitary

 napkins, and other similar personal products or materials.

 (c) Each LEA and public charter school shall provide feminine hygiene products,

 at no charge, in all women's and girls' bathrooms, in all locker rooms, and with the

 school nurse in each eligible school building where instruction is provided, excluding

 bathrooms and locker rooms that are specifically designated for teacher or staff use.

 The feminine hygiene products provided pursuant to this section are for student use

 only.

 (d) The department of education may develop policies and provide guidance to

LEAs and public charter schools to assist local boards of education and public charter

school governing bodies in complying with the requirements of this section.

SECTION 2. This act takes effect July 1, 2025, the public welfare requiring it.
</bill_text>

<summary>
The bill would replace Tennessee Code Annotated section 49-6-417 with the Menstrual Hygiene Products Accessibility Act, effective July 1, 2025. Each local education agency and public charter school would have to provide menstrual hygiene products at no charge in every women’s and girls’ bathroom and locker room, and through the school nurse, in each eligible school building where instruction is provided. An eligible school is a public senior high school, including a public charter school. Products are for student use only, and the requirement excludes bathrooms and locker rooms designated specifically for teachers or staff. The bill defines these products to include tampons, panty liners, menstrual cups, sanitary napkins, and similar products or materials. The Department of Education could develop policies and offer guidance to help schools comply.
</summary>

assessments.summary_quote: An eligible school is a public senior high school, including a public charter school.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the public senior high school limitation and inclusion of public charter schools. The statutory definition cross-reference is not essential here.

assessments.summary_quote: The bill defines these products to include tampons, panty liners, menstrual cups, sanitary napkins, and similar products or materials.
assessments.rationale: Includes the listed examples but omits the broader definition covering products designed for menstruation or other genital-tract secretions.

assessments.summary_quote: Each local education agency and public charter school would have to provide menstrual hygiene products at no charge in every women’s and girls’ bathroom and locker room, and through the school nurse, in each eligible school building where instruction is provided. An eligible school is a public senior high school, including a public charter school. Products are for student use only, and the requirement excludes bathrooms and locker rooms designated specifically for teachers or staff.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the responsible entities, free provision, instructional-building scope, nurse access, and staff-only exception. However, its wording limits locker rooms to women’s and girls’ locker rooms rather than conveying the bill’s requirement for all locker rooms other than those designated for teachers or staff.

assessments.summary_quote: Products are for student use only
assessments.rationale: Expressly conveys the student-only use restriction.

assessments.summary_quote: The Department of Education could develop policies and offer guidance to help schools comply.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the department’s discretionary authority to develop policies and provide compliance guidance, using schools as shorthand for the covered school entities and their governing bodies.
